observations: body L1-L3: the hyphen of «pre-» prints as a dot. «Schiaparelli» is letter-spaced; the dash after «delineavit.» measures 8.8 pt.

body L3-L8: the Arabic is set as printed, with its vowel signs and the shadda over the lām of كلّ; «الى», «على» and «فنرى» are printed without the dots of the yā. The words الى هذا الموضع فوصفنا stand in the Arabic text, vol. III, p. 210, L2, as Nallino says. The sentence of the translation that the correction concerns is p. 139, L20 («Quoniam ad hunc nostri libri locum pervenimus»); «l. 10» (L6) is printed for l. 20, here and in the addenda (Part I, p. LXXII: «139,10, emendandum sicut p. 321 docui.»). The record of p. 139 notes the correction.

body L22-L36: heavy brackets open and close Schiaparelli's addition, from «Indici» (L22) to «Schiaparelli.» (L36); the dash before it measures 10.2 pt. «al–Battānī» (L28, L33, L35) is not letter-spaced; its dashes measure 5.3, 5.2 and 5.2 pt. The c of «indicem» (L30) prints as a blot. The examples of the use of the armillary sphere are on p. 142 of the translation, as printed.
body L37: the dash after «c)» measures 9.6 pt; «143–144» has a long dash (5.3 pt). The triquetrum is described on pp. 143-144 of the translation.

body L38-L45: a speck stands before «Triquetrum» (L38). «al–Battānī» (L39), «Barhebraeus» and «Nau» are letter-spaced. The transliterations are set as printed; the dashes of «al–ʿiḍādah», «aṭ–ṭawīlah», «al–ʿiḍādatāni», «aṭ–ṭawīlatāni», «ash–» and «–shuʿbatayn» measure 5.4, 5.3, 5.4, 5.3, 5.2 and 5.9 pt, the dash of «ash–» being set again at the head of L41. The Syriac words are printed in the Serto script with their vowel signs; the edition sets them in an Estrangela type. The gathering signature 41 stands at the foot of the page.
source_authority: Controlling master page image. Embedded text is not the authority for a reading.
transcription_convention: Source line breaks, hyphenation, quotation signs and word-level type distinctions retained. L numbers count text-bearing lines.
review_responsibility: Transcribed by Claude from the page images; Greek, Arabic, numbers and signs read on enlarged images. Not reviewed by a person.
